items.stem: How does Flutter render its user interface?

options.text: It draws its own widgets onto a canvas rather than wrapping native platform controls
options.rationale: Correct: Flutter renders widgets with its own engine, which is why the UI looks consistent across platforms.

options.text: It wraps each platform's native UI controls directly
options.rationale: Flutter does not wrap native controls; it draws its own.

options.text: It outputs HTML and CSS for every platform
options.rationale: Flutter renders through its engine, not by emitting HTML/CSS to native apps.

options.text: It requires a separate UI codebase per platform
options.rationale: A single widget codebase targets multiple platforms.

items.explanation: Correct: Flutter renders widgets with its own engine, which is why the UI looks consistent across platforms.

items.stem: Which TWO situations call for a StatefulWidget rather than a StatelessWidget? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A counter whose displayed value changes when tapped
options.rationale: Correct: mutable UI state that changes over the widget's life needs a StatefulWidget.

options.text: A form field that tracks and updates its own input
options.rationale: Correct: tracking changing input over time requires state.

options.text: A label that always shows a fixed string
options.rationale: A fixed label has no changing state and can be stateless.
An unchanging icon needs no state.

items.explanation: Correct: mutable UI state that changes over the widget's life needs a StatefulWidget.

items.stem: A screen fetches data from the network. What must the UI handle besides the success case?

options.text: The loading and error states while and if the request fails
options.rationale: Correct: robust async UIs render loading and error states, not only the success case.

options.text: Nothing; the data always arrives instantly
options.rationale: Network requests take time and can fail, so other states are required.

options.text: Only the error state, never loading
options.rationale: Loading must be shown too while the request is in flight.

options.text: Only a blank screen until done
options.rationale: A blank screen gives no feedback and hides errors.

items.explanation: Correct: robust async UIs render loading and error states, not only the success case.
